Cons:

user_reviews.title: Hyundai Venue – Review
user_reviews.author: Rishabh Tiwari
user_reviews.text:
Hyundai Venue – Ownership Review

I’ve been driving my Hyundai Venue for a while now, and overall, it’s been a great experience. The car offers a comfortable ride, modern features, and a solid build quality that makes every drive enjoyable.

In terms of mileage, I’m getting around 11 km/l in city driving conditions and about 16 km/l on the highway, which is quite decent for a compact SUV in this segment. The engine performance is smooth, and the handling is confident, whether in traffic or on long trips.

The interior feels premium with a well-designed dashboard and comfortable seating. The infotainment system is user-friendly, and connectivity options work seamlessly.

Overall, the Hyundai Venue is a reliable, feature-rich, and stylish choice for both city commutes and highway drives. Definitely a great value for money!

user_reviews.title: Hyundai Venue Honest Review.
user_reviews.author: Akshat
user_reviews.text:
New New Hyundai Venue is really a fantastic car to have in terms of premium ownership experience with decent after sales service .  Starting with the engine performance of vehicle is outside with 1.0 TGDI especially in manual transmission with nice to drive and very engaging,  but I would suggest while purchasing venue during its service intervals use fully synthetic engine oil shell helix ultra 0w30 api sp optional product by hyundai little expensive but most best engine oil for turbo engine for high Revving and cold starts rather than regular servo engine oil 0w20 api sn plus is just Ok average performance it gives ideal if you change engine oil at 7500kms , overall engine feels powerful and very refined even with 3cylinder engine there's almost no turbo lag otherwise other engines like Kylaq and 3xo tgdi have significant turbo lag and  I would suggest using 95 octane premium fuel enhances it's fuel efficiency and performance. 6 speed manual transmission is very sleek and very joy to drive extremely smooth and satisfying slotting . Driving dynamics were decent but suspension is a little soft in the new one but still feels decently stable on highway and corners but steering feedback and braking is extremely good and nice one of the best. So on long trips it feels very comfortable both for driver and passengers because of soft suspension and overall interior feels very airy and comfortable with dual tone theme and seats are well-cushioned holds really very well and rear seats with 2 step reclining give seat comfort like a sedan
Boot space of 375 litre feels decent for carrying luggage and suitable for longer trips its decently wide and has good space
From safety point of view standard 6 airbags and enhanced reinforced New k1 platform makes it exceptionally safe as seen in kia syros crash test scored 5 stars so same goes with the venue it is safe and has tons of safety features including ADAS level 2 makes very convincing on Highways but not in cities it may scare sometimes needs to turn off overall exterior looks are very nice it clearly stands out and feels presentable,  futuristic but still looks very nice very sporty
And it's new smart keys with signature Hyundai shell in Matte finish seriously feels extremely upmarket and even more premium than entry level luxury cars . Bose surround sound system seriously feels very soothing to listen and has an exceptional quality of music it offers with different tuning according to your listening. 
Overall New venue is very reliable very safe and very premium and after sales service experience will be good  
Highly recommend for someone who's searching a car under 10 to 15 lakhs and this time it seems more premium than its own manufacturer model like creta

user_reviews.title: My Experience with the Hyundai Venue.
user_reviews.author: Ankit Choudhary
user_reviews.variant: HX 10 Diesel 1.5L Turbo Automatic (TC) Dual Tone [2025-2026]
user_reviews.text:
It’s been a almost 2 year with my Venue, and I’m genuinely happy with it. The car looks premium, drives smooth, and feels solid on the road.
I use it mostly in Delhi traffic, and the AT variant makes driving super easy — no jerks, smooth gear shifts, and great comfort.

Mileage is around 12–13 km/l in city and 16–17 km/l on highways, which is decent. The interior feels classy, AC is powerful, and features like the sunroof, wireless Android Auto, and cruise control make it fun to drive.

Only downside — boot space could’ve been bigger, and I avoided the DCT version since it can heat up in traffic.

Overall, Venue is a perfect all-rounder — stylish, reliable, and comfortable for daily use.

user_reviews.title: Perfect Blend of Power, Mileage, and Comfort – Hyundai Venue SX Diesel
user_reviews.author: akshay Chavan
user_reviews.text:
I recently purchased the Hyundai Venue SX Diesel, and after driving it for a while, I’m very satisfied with the overall experience. The 1.5L diesel engine is smooth, refined, and powerful enough for both city and highway driving. Gear shifts are light, and the torque delivery makes overtaking effortless. I’m getting a fuel efficiency of around 20–22 km/l, which is excellent for a compact SUV.

The ride comfort is impressive — the suspension handles rough patches well, and the cabin feels stable even at higher speeds. Inside, the car feels premium with a modern dashboard, comfortable seats, and good quality materials. The touchscreen infotainment system is responsive, and features like cruise control, climate control, and rear camera add great convenience.

In terms of safety, it has dual airbags, ABS with EBD, rear parking sensors, and a solid build quality, giving good confidence on long drives. The design looks stylish and bold, especially the front grille and LED DRLs.

Overall, the Hyundai Venue SX Diesel is a great package of performance, comfort, and practicality. It’s an ideal SUV for those who want efficiency and features without compromising on looks or comfort.
